My top best selling products on Etsy✨🩷 After 6 years of selling print on demand products through Printify + Etsy, these are some of the products that have consistently been best sellers for me: • Sweatshirts My favorites are the Gildan 18000 + Comfort Colors 1566. They’re super versatile, come in tons of colors, and there are now even more ways to customize them with DTG, DTF, embroidery AND some new printing options from Printify. Glitter puff print?!! More on that soon👀👀 • Phone Cases One of my favorite evergreen products because people are constantly switching out their cases. They’re also SO easy to design with patterns, photos, personalized designs and more. Plus, they’re especially great around new phone releases! • Glass Tumbler Cups These have been a bestseller for me ever since Printify released them! The prints come out so crisp and vibrant, they include a lid + straw, and they’re perfect for personalized gifts. And yes, even though they’re glass, I’ve sold a ton and have rarely had shipping issues! • Hardcover Journals Simple, easy to customize and such a good gift product. Patterns and personalized designs work especially well, and the print quality is SO good. I own way too many myself! • Embroidered Hats Especially the vintage + denim hats! I love the color options, the embroidery comes out super clean, and these have consistently sold really well in my shop. • Mugs A classic for a reason, but I like choosing mugs that stand out a little more while someone is scrolling. The accent color mugs + latte mugs are two of my favorites! The best part? These are all evergreen products, meaning they can sell year round, not just during one specific season! 🤭How to make money online selling products on Etsy you didn't make yourself using the done for you designs & print on demand method!  👇🏼Read for a step by step!  🙌🏼 How Print On Demand Works:  1. Do Some Quick Product Research - Look for popular items people are buying, like wall art, t-shirts, sweatshirts, phone cases, candles, mugs, or tote bags.   - Use tools like erank, Google Trends or browse online shops to see what's trending. I also look for inspo on Pinterest all the time! I like to use Everbee to see how much money a product is making on Etsy.  2. Create Your Design  - Get done for you designs on ctrl-alt-design.com  - Or create your own. Make your design fun, eye-catching, or niche-specific. Keep it simple and high-quality!   3. Sign Up on Printify  - Create a free account & make sure you connect your account to a store. Examples being Etsy or Shopify. You are walked through how to do this when you sign up, don’t worry it’s easy and fast.  4. Choose a Product on Printify   - Browse the product catalog for posters, t-shirts, hoodies, candles, hats, mugs, phone cases & etc.   - Select the product you want to sell.   5. Upload Your Design   - Click on the product to customize it.   - Upload your design.   - Position and resize it to fit the product nicely.   6. Fill Out Listing Details  - Write a catchy product title and description with keywords.   - Set your price (consider costs and your profit margin).   7. Publish Your Product  - Remember to connect your online store (Shopify, Etsy, etc.) with Printful . This makes it so whenever you make a sale, Printify knows instantly so it can print the design on the product for you and send it to the customer for you!  - Publish your product so it’s live and ready for customers.   8. Market Your Product - Share your product on social media, use Pinterest, create ads, or tell friends. Make videos of your product or make Pinterest pins.  - Focus on your target audience to attract more buyers. Those top sellers on Etsy have some things in common 👀 I’ve been selling on Etsy for 6 years and I’ll be honest with you, there isn’t a magic formula. Anyone who tells you otherwise, is probably trying to sell you something. BUT!! there are things I see top Etsy sellers do over and over again that I believe 100% helps them make more sales: 1) They use DATA. This is a big one that so many new sellers overlook. Top sellers aren’t just randomly deciding what niche they want to sell in or what phrase to put on their shirt. They use tools like Everbee, erank, or RankHero to find profitable niches BEFORE they put a single product in their Etsy shop. They also use these tools to optimize their titles, tags, and general SEO. Stop guessing, start using DATA 🙌 2) They study design trends. Top sellers have their finger on the pulse of what is currently trending. They use Pinterest, other Etsy shops, trends reports, and just in general their eyes and minds when they are out shopping to start noticing patterns of what is currently trending and then they apply those trends to their designs! 🥳 3) They use Print on Demand. Not all of them, but most of the top shops I see are using Printify as their supplier so that they can sell more products! 🙌 When you can test out different designs and styles and products without the upfront costs, you are giving yourself so many more chances to be found by your target audience. Print on demand is a game changer for Etsy sellers and I talk a LOT about how you can use Printify in your Etsy shop! 💖 4) Their mockups are on POINT. This is something I will never stop shouting from the rooftops because it is THAT important. Good mockups can make or break your Etsy shop - get some good ones!! 5) They don’t give up!! They test and test and test and take any data and information they get and apply it to more designs, more products, and that eventually leads to more sales. Keep learning, keep growing, and don’t give up because YOU CAN DO THIS!! Etsy SEO has changed and if you’re still treating Etsy search as simply “put your keywords in the title”, you’re missing a lot. Etsy is increasingly using AI to understand what shoppers are searching for and what your listings actually contain. That means things like your attributes, tags, listing images and the information surrounding your product can all help Etsy understand where your listing belongs. In this video I go through 5 Etsy SEO and listing optimisation tips that I think a lot of sellers overlook including one involving your listing images and alt text that can also help Google understand your products. I also show you why you shouldn't just repeat the same keyword across all 13 tags, and how Etsy Marketplace Insights can give you actual search data to find new keyword opportunities. If you sell on Etsy and you're trying to get more views on your listings, these are the sorts of things I'd be looking at before blindly rewriting hundreds of titles. And that's basically what The Messy Seller is about: digging into the stuff behind Etsy search, testing what actually makes sense, and separating useful Etsy SEO from the advice that just gets repeated because someone said it once.
